newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse eases down on low volumes.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse eases down on low volumes.

text.p: The Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) eased marginally as cautious investors traded low volumes, bourse floor traders said on Friday.
The 30-share index shed 4.42 points to close at 3425.22, with turnover increasing to 27.8 million shillings traded on 672,750 shares from 12.76 million shillings traded on 262,085 shares.
"Generally speaking the NSE's decline was not connected to share prices," said a senior dealer, saying the fall was caused by low volumes in non-blue chip shares.

He said investors were still cautious as they recovered from a body blow dealt to local and foreign speculators' confidence by the International Monetary Fund when it cancelled a key aid package to Kenya on July 31.

Bourse officials said investors were keeping a watchful eye on newly-listed Athi River Mining on Friday. But what was expected to be the day's main feature turned out to be of little interest with its share price hovering at 12.5 shillings.
"Athi River did not trade at a significant premium," said a bourse floor dealer. "We were hoping it might hit 18 or 20."
The new arrival ended up dealing 27,500 shares at between 12.35-12.6 shillings, to close at 12.5.

The Kenyan shilling's decline since the end of July has meant windfall gains for exporters and boosted interest in the agricultural sector in the last few days, with 58,300 shares changing hands there over the week.
Rea Vipingo moved 20,620 shares on Friday, with prices ranging from 8.7-9.0 shillings. No deals were made in Sasini Tea and Coffee, which had traded steadily at 81.50 throughout the week.
Uchumi Supermarkets dealt 68,185 shares, to close unchanged at 38.5. Kenya Airways traded 132,425 shares at eight shillings unchanged.
National Industrial Credit was the week's main feature on the finance board, trading over 497,000 shares at between 48.25-53.5 shillings.
On Friday Barclays Bank moved 9,237 shares at between 108-111 shillings from 109.
Apart from Athi River Mining, there were few big trades in the industrial sector. Crown Berger moved 1,500 shares and closed unchanged at 11.1 shillings.
Trade was brisk in the bond sector, with 330.1 million shillings worth of the fourth issue of the Central Bank of Kenya floating-rate treasury bond traded at 102.8900 percent from 102.8850 percent.
The third issue moved 50,000 shillings at 102.0000 percent, from 102.5000 percent.
